description: Takes a video and a description of what to change, and generates the SAME clip with those changes applied - different characters, different clothes, a different setting - while the camera move, the timing, the framing and the performers' motion stay exactly as they were. Returns the new job's id immediately. WHEN: the user wants to restyle, recast or reskin footage they already have, rather than generate something new. 'Make the crowd elderly', 'put them all in suits', 'make it snow' - the source clip decides what HAPPENS, the prompt decides what it LOOKS like. This is not `generate_video` with a reference: nothing here is invented from scratch. THE SOURCE CLIP MUST BE 3 TO 10 SECONDS. That one is a hard bound: a longer clip is REFUSED before anything is charged, so cut a long video into sub-10-second pieces and edit each one - the pieces are independent jobs and their results can be joined afterwards. Frame size and frame rate are NOT bounds you have to meet: a clip outside the model's 720-2160px or 24-60fps range is resized and re-timed server-side rather than refused. THE PROVIDER SCREENS THE SOURCE CLIP FOR REAL PEOPLE. Footage of identifiable real people - a music video, a film, a clip of a person off the internet - can be refused as a likeness, and a refused job is REFUNDED in full. That is a property of the footage, not of the prompt, so rewording does not get past it; the way through is a source clip with no real identifiable faces in it. THE CARD: this call has ALREADY put the aicut card in front of the user, and it fills in the finished media on its own. Do NOT call `show_generation` for this job - that adds a duplicate card; it is only for bringing back an EARLIER generation. HOW TO WAIT: call `wait_for_generation` with this job's id and `media` - it waits server-side and opens no card. While it answers `terminal: false`, wait `poll_after_seconds` and call it again; when `terminal: true`, tell the user in ONE short line what came out. Do not poll `get_video` / `get_image` / `get_audio` instead or spawn timers, and do NOT tell the user the generation is running in between. IF YOU CANNOT RENDER AN AICUT CARD (a terminal or plain SDK client), give the user the `url` from the wait result - aicut cannot see which clients render cards. TIMING: a video usually finishes in 1-3 minutes, and can take up to about 6. Do not assume it failed before then, and do not spawn timers or background shells to wait: call `wait_for_generation` (it waits server-side for up to 15 seconds per call), wait its `poll_after_seconds` and call it again, and stop when it answers `terminal: true`. `get_video` is a single immediate read for one job's raw fields - it is not the waiting loop and must not be polled in one. COST: this spends the user's tokens, and the price is a per-second rate that depends on the resolution, times the LENGTH - the SOURCE clip's length by default (1080p costs more than 720p, and a 10-second clip costs about three times a 3-second one). The clip's length is MEASURED BY THE SERVER from the file itself, never taken from anything you say - that measurement is the price and the charge. A clip aicut cannot measure (a WebM, or a file whose header it cannot read) is REFUSED with nothing charged; re-encode it to MP4 and try again. Sending `reference_images` changes what the length is priced from: with no `duration` sent it still falls back to the source clip's length, but a `duration` you send there IS what is priced and charged - it is not merely descriptive. Pass `estimate_only: true` first to get the exact price. REFERENCE IMAGES (optional): pass `reference_images` to additionally steer the result with up to a few pictures - a face, an outfit, a prop the model should draw from instead of inventing. This does NOT change what happens in the clip; the source clip still decides the motion, the timing and the camera. Sending any reference image switches on a second provider mode that also accepts an explicit `duration` (the output length is otherwise still the source clip's) and `aspect_ratio` (otherwise inherited from the source clip) - set either only when the user asked for a specific value. An EXTERNAL url is downloaded and stored on the account before it can be measured, which uses one of the account's daily media-ingest slots. Quoting and then creating from the SAME url costs that once, not twice - aicut reuses what it already imported - and a url already on the account costs nothing at all. SPENDS TOKENS: quote it first (`estimate_only: true`), state the price IN THE SAME MESSAGE as your ask, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase - a bare 'yes' counts only as the direct answer to that priced ask, and an ambiguous one means ask again. The full SPENDING RULES in this server's instructions apply here. IF THE USER REPORTS A CHARGE OR STEP THEY DID NOT EXPECT: re-read your own tool calls and say which you made; aicut cards cannot spend (full rule in this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: `idempotency_key` is optional. Reusing a key REPLAYS the job it first created (even with different settings), so never reuse one to make another generation; the full rules are in this server's instructions (IDEMPOTENCY). OUTPUT: JSON for you to read. Tell the user the media URL plus a one-line summary; do not paste raw JSON, job ids or internal field names.

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio (for example `9:16`). Only meaningful alongside `reference_images` - without it the output inherits the source clip's own shape. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

duration.description: Output length in seconds. Only meaningful alongside `reference_images` - without it the output is always the source clip's own length. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

estimate_only.description: Price these exact settings and create nothing. Returns the token cost, the account balance, and whether the balance covers it. Costs nothing and changes nothing.

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry-safety key. Read the IDEMPOTENCY note in this tool's description before using one - a reused key returns the first job instead of making a new one.

prompt.description: What to CHANGE about the clip. Describe the replacement, not the whole scene: the camera, the timing and the motion are kept from the source, so directions about them are wasted. Name what each thing in frame should become instead.

reference_images.description: URLs of up to a few images to steer the result with - a face, an outfit, a prop to draw from instead of inventing one. Same URL rules as `source_video`. Sending this switches the request onto kling-o3's `references` mode, which also accepts `duration` and `aspect_ratio` below; omit it entirely for a plain edit.

resolution.description: Output resolution. 1080p costs more per second. Never set this to save the user tokens or to make a generation cheaper - set it only when the user explicitly asked for this value, and never carry it over from an earlier request.

source_video.description: URL of the video to edit - 3 to 10 seconds long. Either a URL an earlier generation or upload on THIS account returned, or a genuinely external public https URL - aicut downloads it, size-caps it and stores it on the account first. An aicut-hosted URL belonging to a DIFFERENT account is refused.
